assumptions: Local execution environment and recorded versions are accurate.
limitations: External runtime, security, legal and human qualification remain outside this package.
confidence: high for repository-local exercised evidence; low for external production qualification
independentVerificationStatus: internal role-separated adversarial validation; external certification pending

risks.risk: No live PostgreSQL primary/standby, pool-isolation, failover or PITR qualification.
risks.control: Static contracts and target runner; production blocked.

risks.risk: No independently qualified untrusted-code boundary.
risks.control: Untrusted host execution blocked.

risks.risk: No authorized KMS/HSM or external monotonic witness.
risks.control: Attested protocol rehearsal only.

risks.risk: No measured human product-value evidence.
risks.control: Five-task consented protocol; human-value claims prohibited.

risks.risk: No external penetration or licensing review.
risks.control: Production promotion blocked.

risks.risk: Registry mirror allowlisting does not establish mirror governance or provenance.
risks.control: Exact host allowlist, integrity and no install scripts; external mirror review remains required.

risks.risk: Single-host file replay is not a multi-host consensus or durable-database guarantee.
risks.control: Authority limited to local package; multi-host promotion blocked.

risks.risk: Operational telemetry or action evidence could grow or leak sensitive values.
risks.control: Bounded retention/cardinality, allowlists, hashing, redaction and digest verification.

risks.risk: Archive portability can silently depend on filesystem modes or omitted inputs.
risks.control: Normalized archive policy, explicit interpreters, manifest and malicious archive self-tests.

risks.risk: Fifty non-critical tests are not individually mapped in the selected critical-invariant catalog.
risks.control: Full suite remains authoritative; expand mapping only where decision value justifies it.

risks.risk: Model or orchestrator dependency substitution could attempt authority escalation or malformed change admission.
risks.control: Assistant independently verifies receipt signature, identity, proposal-only ceiling and tool semantics; output remains review-only.

risks.risk: Fixture model tests do not establish production model quality, latency, privacy or provider resilience.
risks.control: No production model-value claim; external provider qualification and human pilot required.

risks.risk: Registry advisory endpoint failure could hide vulnerability status.
risks.control: Three-state audit classification and explicit environment-blocked qualification.

risks.risk: Sensitive repository targets could bypass agent policy through lockfile-specific branch logic.
risks.control: Direct sensitive-target rejection plus adversarial tests and authentic mutation kill.

risks.risk: Coverage excludes some subprocess and environment-only paths from the in-process percentage.
risks.control: Correctness lanes still execute those paths; coverage scope and exclusions are explicitly reported.

risks.risk: Original source archives and licenses are not present in the v32.1 workspace, so direct source-code adoption cannot be independently requalified.
risks.control: Use bounded behavioral reimplementation with explicit source lineage; do not claim direct code adoption.

risks.risk: External readiness remains below the production floor because PostgreSQL failover/PITR, HSM/KMS, multi-host propagation and independent review are absent.
risks.control: Production promotion blocked by the external-readiness scorecard axis.

risks.risk: Human and commercial value are not yet measured.
risks.control: Value hypotheses and claim-forbidden policy require a consented comparative pilot.

risks.risk: Local performance may regress as test and proof depth grows.
risks.control: Normalized per-test performance budget and stability tracking.

risks.risk: Locally generated or simulated material could be mislabeled as external qualification evidence.
risks.control: Observed-only envelope, independent reviewer identity, verified signature and exact source/artifact digest binding.

risks.risk: Human pilot evidence could expose personal data or be collected without valid consent.
risks.control: Use pseudonymous participant IDs, explicit consent, preregistration and minimum-data retention outside the release archive.

risks.risk: A nominally independent reviewer may have organizational or financial conflicts.
risks.control: Distinct reviewer organization, conflict declaration, signed scope-specific verdict and procurement independence review.

risks.risk: Qualification thresholds could be selected after observing results.
risks.control: Thresholds are carried in preregistered evidence and evaluated deterministically.

risks.risk: Optimization pressure could inflate scores by relabeling simulations or readiness as external truth.
risks.control: Score derivation preserves human, HSM, witness, PostgreSQL, independent review and multi-host blockers; project scores remain capped.

risks.risk: Adding metrics could dilute promotion-critical core axes through averaging.
risks.control: The holistic score fixes core axes at 70 percent and external production blockers remain non-compensable.

risks.risk: Repository-local observability and capacity evidence could be misrepresented as production telemetry or cloud cost.
risks.control: Reports state local-only limits and external collector, provider billing and multi-host SLO remain unqualified.

risks.risk: Accessibility confidence remains limited without consented observation by representative human participants.
risks.control: Static accessibility contracts are enforced while humanObserved remains false and the human-study limitation is explicit.

risks.risk: Dependency health could become stale between local validations.
risks.control: Exact pinning, integrity and replacement tests are local gates; continuous advisory monitoring remains an explicit external limitation.

risks.risk: A large number of correlated tests could be mistaken for independent proof.
risks.control: Proof diversity requires distinct techniques, oracles, environments and defect classes.

risks.risk: Happy-path integration tests could conceal timeout, replay, tamper, concurrency and rollback defects.
risks.control: Integration contracts and fault campaigns make negative-path obligations mandatory.

risks.risk: An automated local evaluator could be mistaken for production promotion authority.
risks.control: Governed release assurance hard-codes production promotion as blocked and reports external blockers separately.

risks.risk: A popular GitHub repository or mutable Action tag could be treated as trusted code without immutable provenance.
risks.control: Adapter-only intake, full-SHA workflow pins and no vendoring or runtime network authority.

risks.risk: Synthetic SARIF, attestation, policy, formal or fuzz metadata could be mistaken for executed assurance evidence.
risks.control: Evidence gates require observed state and exact digest binding; current external tools remain NOT_EXECUTED.

risks.risk: Large quantities of correlated local proof could falsely close human, external or signed claims.
risks.control: Adversarial claim roast requires independent oracles, environments and external collection where applicable.

risks.risk: CI workflow dependencies could be compromised or receive excessive credentials.
risks.control: Workflow security gate requires immutable SHAs, checkout credential isolation, read-only permissions and bounded artifacts.

risks.risk: Local signatures and witness evidence are not externally transparent or independently governed.
risks.control: Classify as local-only, keep production blocked, and require external signer transparency and witness independence.

risks.risk: Archived PASS reports may be mistaken for evidence from the current validation attempt when source and environment digests are unchanged.
risks.control: Require a fresh run directory, atomic execution ledger, ordered successful steps, artifact hashes, sizes, modification times and exact run identity before finalization.

risks.risk: Cross-tenant or stale semantic cache reuse could disclose or substitute results.
risks.control: Exact tenant workload operation sensitivity source policy authority and freshness binding; restricted semantic reuse is denied and mutation-tested.

risks.risk: Cost optimization could remove resilience reserve or provider independence.
risks.control: Exact optimizer fails closed unless compute database witness backup reserve provider and failure-domain floors all pass.

risks.risk: Proposal-only capacity plans do not prove real host scaling, provider custody, failover or production SLOs.
risks.control: Keep production blocked and require authorized adapters plus independent multi-host qualification.

risks.risk: Binary parser ambiguity or polyglot content could create false artifact identity or unsafe model context.
risks.control: Magic and structure cross-checks, strict policy, bounded context, domain-separated chunks, Merkle root, fuzzing, mutation and independent Python verification.

risks.risk: Model-provider benchmark or marketing claims could be mistaken for platform proof.
risks.control: Comparative assurance separates official claims from observed current execution and blocks world-best status without all critical observed dimensions.

risks.risk: Local model orchestration and binary proof do not establish independent multi-host production superiority.
risks.control: Keep production and world-best claims blocked pending external comparative workload, independent host, human value and six qualification gates.

risks.risk: Synthetic model outputs or self-declared keys could be presented as an external frontier benchmark.
risks.control: Out-of-band provider and judge trust, signed submissions, blind commitments, independent review, complete matrix and explicit dry-run verdict.

risks.risk: A WASM module could gain undeclared authority or be composed through ambiguous or cyclic interfaces.
risks.control: Exact WIT imports and exports, capability grants, bounded filesystem and network scope, independent review and composition graph validation.

risks.risk: Local process simulations do not establish independent multi-host production behavior or WASI runtime isolation.
risks.control: Production remains blocked pending externally pinned multi-host evidence and independent runtime qualification.

risks.risk: Malformed or hidden-memory WebAssembly could evade stable runtime classification or memory accounting.
risks.control: Compile and inspect exports before worker launch, require one named memory export, enforce timeout and measured memory limits, and kill causal mutations.

risks.risk: A model provider could self-attest API transport or substitute a response after execution.
risks.control: Require independently authorized signed transport observations bound to request, response, provider and external response identifiers.

risks.risk: Single-machine process failover does not establish independent-host, provider or failure-domain resilience.
risks.control: Keep production blocked and execute the same challenge across independently operated external hosts.

risks.risk: A compatible component could gain authority through untrusted identity, interface drift, broad transport or self-review.
risks.control: Exact admission policy binds SPIFFE trust domain, UDS, interfaces, digests, resource limits, egress and reviewer independence.

risks.risk: One implementation could become a hidden monopoly despite portable APIs.
risks.control: Topology requires full building-block coverage, organization diversity, concentration ceilings and measured substitution coverage.

risks.risk: Local envelope adapters do not prove actual Dapr, SPIRE, OPA, OpenTelemetry, Wasmtime or CloudNativePG behavior.
risks.control: Keep production blocked and execute pinned runtime profiles on independently operated hosts.

risks.risk: Retries can amplify side effects or create unbounded latency and load.
risks.control: Compiler rejects retry without idempotency and enforces attempts resource and worst-case duration ceilings.

risks.risk: Workflow replay can duplicate effects or accept mixed and tampered history.
risks.control: Sequence hash-chain identity transition and unique effect ownership checks fail closed.

risks.risk: Telemetry savings can discard the exact traces required for security and reliability evidence.
risks.control: Mandatory error security and high-latency traces are retained and budget overrun is explicit.

risks.risk: Local identity and database observations do not prove SPIRE federation or CloudNativePG HA and PITR.
risks.control: Production remains blocked pending independently observed external daemon qualification.

risks.risk: Distinct local processes and loopback HTTP do not prove independent external administration, public HTTPS durability or clock independence.
risks.control: Keep production blocked and execute V33.36 on separately administered externally retrievable hosts with pinned clock and certificate evidence.

risks.mitigation: Require signed host evidence from two independent topology auditors.

risks.risk: The interoperability proof uses locally generated adapter modules attestations providers monitors and sites and has not run on independently administered external HSM infrastructure.

risks.risk: The capsule tarballs were repacked from exact preinstalled packages rather than fetched with original registry signatures.

risks.risk: Local candidate descriptors and deterministic canary metrics may not predict compatibility or reliability of a real independently sourced package release.

risks.risk: Local target-version fixtures and deterministic canary metrics may not predict real coupled-package compatibility or production behavior.

risks.risk: Local multi-process failover does not prove independent host, clock or durable-storage administration.
risks.control: Keep the verdict local-only and require external host, clock and journal qualification before production authority.

risks.risk: Local mutual-authentication fixtures and builtin scans could be mislabeled as independently administered external intake.

risks.risk: Queue state or reviewer collusion could be mistaken for independently verified external evidence.
risks.mitigation: Bind approvals to original v33.50 receipt signatures, require reviewer separation and keep external readiness false without twenty-two attestations.

risks.risk: Stale workers, split journal replicas or overloaded queues could create duplicate or divergent operations.
risks.mitigation: Use lease fencing, witness-qualified takeover, exact-byte replica receipts, idempotency keys, pressure hysteresis and full audit replay.

risks.risk: Collocated stores, clock skew, split view, premature failover or overload bypass could invalidate persistence qualification.
risks.mitigation: Require identity separation, exact-byte receipts, two-clock quorum, two partition observers, rejection thresholds, hysteresis and site-loss replay.

risks.risk: Nonce replay, process reuse, auditor collusion, drill substitution or non-portable evidence could create a false readiness verdict.

risks.risk: Share exposure, custody-ledger fork, controller collusion, infected media or revocation bypass could expose evidence.
risks.mitigation: Use 2-of-3 shares, monotonic ledger, dual control, quarantine scanning and irreversible quorum revocation.

risks.risk: Ledger fork, stale authority resurrection, compromised shares or emergency-quorum abuse could expose evidence.
risks.mitigation: Use three replicas, fencing, independent witnesses, rotation, containment, one-time emergency quorum and terminal expiration.
